clue.text: Big return from the sale of blubber?

definitions.text: Big return from the sale of blubber?

parts.words: Big return from the sale of blubber?
parts.note: a large gain on a deal, read again as the takings from selling whale fat

explanation.surface: A whaler wonders how much money a cargo of blubber will fetch.
explanation.definitionFit: A large gain is a fat one, and money made from selling fat is literally the same phrase.

clue.text: In truth it is so religious

definitions.meaning: the Hebrew word means truly or verily, as in the Gospels' 'verily I say'
said at the end of a prayer to mean 'so be it'

explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrew word means 'truly' and closes prayers as an affirmation, 'so be it'.

clue.text: Proper blend of tea for a high churchman

parts.note: prim means proper or prudishly correct

indicators.note: a blend mixes things together, so the letters of tea are mixed up

explanation.surface: A tea merchant mixes a suitably refined brew for a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blend of' is the anagram signal, and 'tea' is its fodder; the surface's tea blend is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: An archbishop, the most senior cleric of a province, bears this title.

clue.text: Craft operatives who twist one's arm

indicators.note: twisting the words bends their letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Hired heavies who twist people's arms to get their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twist' rearranges ONES and ARM. 'Craft' is a boat, not a trade or guile, and the 'operatives' work the oars.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowers are the people who work a boat by its oars.

clue.text: 22 militants blimpish at heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so the central letters of blimpish are taken

explanation.surface: Some Black militants turn out to be pompous reactionaries underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 is 22-across, BLACK. 'Blimpish' means like Colonel Blimp, a cartoon pompous British reactionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Zulu regiments of warriors were called by this name, so they are Black fighters.

clue.text: Sum originally expended on the purchase of a monogram?

definitions.text: Sum originally expended on the purchase of a monogram?

parts.words: Sum originally expended on the purchase of a monogram?
parts.note: first money spent on a venture, read again as money laid out on initials

explanation.surface: Someone tots up what they first paid for a personalised monogram.
explanation.definitionFit: The start-up cost of a venture is the first spend; a monogram is made of initials, so buying one is an outlay on initials.

clue.text: Canvassers who revel in the joys of spring!

definitions.text: Canvassers who revel in the joys of spring!

parts.words: Canvassers who revel in the joys of spring!
parts.note: people who bounce on a springy canvas sheet, not vote-seekers enjoying the season

explanation.surface: Election campaigners are delighted that spring has come.
explanation.definitionFit: Bouncers on a rebound frame jump on a canvas bed held by springs.

clue.text: Middling account of company proceedings

parts.note: a statement of a firm's business issued partway through the year, not a mediocre one

explanation.surface: A shareholder grumbles that the firm's account of its business was only so-so.
explanation.definitionFit: Companies issue a half-year statement of trading between annual accounts, so it comes in the middle.

clue.text: It gives relish in breaking into a shanty

indicators.note: one word forcing its way inside another, as a burglar breaks into a house

parts.note: a shanty is a sailors' work song, a sea song

explanation.surface: A singer brightens a sailors' song by bursting in on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking into' is the container signal; the answer splits the sea song after its sixth letter to admit the little word.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt, pepper and herbs add flavour, the relish, to food.

clue.text: Most of us rely on them for information

definitions.text: Most of us rely on them for information

parts.words: Most of us rely on them for information
parts.note: the press, radio and television that serve the general public with news

explanation.surface: A plain statement that the public gets its news from somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers, radio and television reach the whole population, the 'mass' being most of us.

clue.text: Takes a set dish?

indicators.note: to dish is to ruin or wreck, so the letters of the words are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone chooses the set menu at a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' rearranges A SET. It reads as a noun for food but works as a verb meaning wreck.
explanation.definitionFit: To take food is to consume it, as in 'takes lunch at noon'.

clue.text: Italian city Rex takes his parents round

indicators.note: the parents go round the king, enclosing his letter

parts.note: a child's parents are pa and ma
R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A man named Rex shows his mother and father the sights of an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is the container signal; 'takes his parents round' reads as a guided tour, but the king's letter sits between the two parents.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in Emilia-Romagna, famous for its ham and cheese.

clue.text: Section of Jerusalem made famous by Jane Austen

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some part of Jerusalem was made famous by a novel of Jane Austen.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the title made famous by the novelist; 'made' is part of the hidden run, so the definition reads 'famous by Jane Austen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Austen's 1815 novel is named after its heroine, Miss Woodhouse.

clue.text: A tax haven for copra traders, maybe

parts.note: a toll is a charge or levy

explanation.surface: A levy imposed on dealers in coconut produce.
explanation.walkthrough: Copra is dried coconut kernel, traded from Pacific islands.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring-shaped coral island, where coconut traders might shelter, typically in the Pacific.

clue.text: Gets excited about a point reached in development

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the next piece
excited letters are stirred up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone becomes agitated over how far a project has come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges GETS to STGE, and 'about' wraps it round A.
explanation.definitionFit: A phase or step in a process, as in 'an early stage'.

clue.text: A pay-out in Washington?

indicators.note: the single letter goes inside the word for paying out

parts.note: to settle a bill is to pay it

explanation.surface: Someone receives a payment while in the US capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Washington is the state, not the capital; the question mark marks the city as an example of a place in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest city in the Pacific Northwest state is an example of a place there.

clue.text: Ideas out of the question when I come in with sulphur

indicators.note: the letter enters the phrase, going inside it

parts.note: 'not on' means not allowed, out of the question
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A chemist's ideas are dismissed until someone adds sulphur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come in' puts I inside NOTON, then S follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoughts or concepts, often vague ones.

clue.text: Not the intelligentsia served in Chinese restaurants

definitions.meaning: fools or dimwits, the opposite of clever people
strands of pasta-like dough, a staple dish in Chinese cooking

explanation.definitionFit: A noodle is slang for a simpleton, and long strips of dough are a common Chinese dish.

clue.text: Fresh as a lion in "The Merchant of Venice"

indicators.note: made fresh, the letters are formed into something new

explanation.surface: A new lion appears in a Shakespeare comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Venetian friend of Antonio, one of the minor characters of Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Left to burn smoky fuel

parts.note: to ignite is to set burning

explanation.surface: Leaving a smoky fuel to burn.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown coal, a low-grade fuel that gives off much smoke.

clue.text: Fortune gained the wrong a way in Uttar Pradesh

parts.note: luck means fortune or chance

indicators.note: read the wrong way means reading the word backwards
this word means the letters it governs are turned round, so they are read backwards

parts.note: won means gained or earned

explanation.surface: Someone's fortune was made dishonestly in northern India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' is the reversal signal on the word for gained; Lucknow is the capital of the Indian state, so 'in Uttar Pradesh' defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of the north Indian state is a place in it.

clue.text: Initially it is prepared to defend Anatolia inter alia

definitions.text: Initially it is prepared to defend Anatolia inter alia

indicators.note: at the start of the word the letters lie concealed, near its beginning

explanation.surface: A military alliance stands ready to protect Turkey among other places.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits near the start of Anatolia, the Asian part of Turkey, which the alliance is pledged to defend along with its other members.
explanation.definitionFit: The North Atlantic alliance counts Turkey among its members, so it would defend that land.

clue.text: Second man to go on board

definitions.text: Second man to go on board

parts.words: Second man to go on board
parts.note: in chess the side that moves after White, not a passenger boarding a ship

explanation.surface: A second person boards a ship or plane.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, the dark pieces always move after White, so their player goes second on the board.

clue.text: Rodolfo found her small casual worker extremely cold

definitions.text: Rodolfo found her small casual worker extremely cold

parts.words: Rodolfo found her small casual worker extremely cold
parts.note: in Puccini's opera the poet tells the seamstress her tiny hand is frozen; a hand is also a casual worker

explanation.surface: A man finds his part-time employee standoffish.
explanation.walkthrough: In La Bohème Rodolfo sings 'Che gelida manina' (your tiny hand is frozen) to the seamstress; 'casual worker' is a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of La Bohème is the seamstress whose cold hand the poet Rodolfo takes.

clue.text: Palatial place in Norway

parts.note: the Norwegian city where the royal palace stands, the capital

explanation.surface: A grand residence somewhere in Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian capital is home to the Royal Palace.

clue.text: Very unfair in outlook

parts.note: far from fair-looking, plain of face, and also menacing in prospect, as an outlook turns nasty

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of holding most unjust views.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfair in looks means not handsome, and a threatening prospect is also described this way.

clue.text: Alternations of light and shade

parts.note: the daily cycle of daylight and darkness, not contrasts in a painting

explanation.surface: A painter's chiaroscuro alternates light and shadow.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun's rising and setting give a regular swing between daylight and dark.

clue.text: Facilities not provided for slowcoaches

parts.note: fast roads where slow vehicles such as tractors and learners are banned

explanation.surface: Amenities are denied to people who dawdle.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's fast highways bar slow traffic such as mopeds and learner drivers.
